When He says that He will crush those who bear the heavy yoke, then He remembers as an atonement the destruction of the site of the Sanctuary. The sucklings who praised the Lord at the Sea of Reeds, the promise of the covenant (the circumcision) and the statutes (of the Torah), His holy word, all these does He remember. The memory of those who live austerely (students of the Torah) and study His beautiful sayings, who with their lips provide a substitute for sacrificial bullocks, He does remember. When the books that announce what is hidden, are examined, He remembers in love the wonderful pair of brothers. He remembers the honour of the sanctuary, the place where He, the Beloved, did dwell, where He allowed the Cherubim to rest, the love of our youth He remembers. The basin on its frame, the delightful voice (of the Levites) on the Temple steps, the Almighty recalls them in favour of the discerning on the appointed day of judgment.

blocks.text: On Sabbath.

As it is written through Thy prophet: ‘Then those who fear God speak one to the other and God listens and hears, and it is inscribed in the book of remembrance before Him on behalf of those who fear the Lord and respect His Name’.

The foxes (Egyptians), the destroyers of vineyards, planned to cut off from the vine its root and remembrance. They oppressed them (Israel) with hardship, they cried out to Thee and were saved because of the piety of the forefathers who had been inscribed for remembrance.
As it is written in Thy Torah: ‘God heard their cry, then God remembered His covenant with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob’.

In days of old Thou didst see generations in whom there was no delight. Thou hast let them vanish and perish without a remembrance. One generation hast Thou chosen from among a thousand and allotted them Thy words; for their sake in every generation hast Thou engraved them for remembrance.
As it is written in Thy holy words: ‘He remembers for ever His covenant, the word He commanded for a thousand generations’.

alignment_observations: There are two continuous flows per page, separated by a horizontal rule: weekday זכר תחלת on top, Shabbat אפחד במעשי on the bottom. Weekday runs s282→s284→s286 and ends 'קְרָב'. Shabbat runs s282 'בִּנְדִיבִים'→s284 'דֶּלֶת'. English follows the same split on s283/285/287.
Shabbat verse chain: Gen 8:1 → עשה → Ps 111:4–5 → פנה (s284) → Mal 3:16 → צצו → Ex 2:24 → קדם → Ps 105:8 (s286). The weekday flow has no verses in this range.
English join: s285 ends 'He re-' and s287 begins 'members'. Record as a hyphenated cross-page join (join='He re-|members', no space inserted).
The primary weekday Hebrew had many invented readings, especially s282 lines 1–8 and the s284 stanza heads. Each stanza head prints זֵכֶר, never זְכֹר.
The source distinguishes plene and defective forms of יזכור/לזכור in each instance; I left them as printed rather than standardizing.
Biblical citations are in smaller type without teamim. Source forms are kept where they differ from Tanakh: לְעֹלָם (2×), וּלְחוֹשְׁבֵי, and אֶל רֵעֵהוּ with no maqaf.
Speaker labels do not appear in the English.
verdict: Corrected candidate replacing the primary: about 60 Hebrew word-level corrections; English is unchanged except restoring the printed 'death' on s287. The rubric reading, the speaker-label identity and the listed vowel points still need enlarged-image adjudication. No acceptance claimed.
